Scientist Albert Einstein once said, "Imagination is more important than Knowledge." I strongly agree with this statement due to the reason that a human once used his imagination to create an acknowledging fact. Examples to support my opinion are Problems, Risks, and Experience.

For nearly every Problem is a Solution; But How did we find out? Throughout History Humans have had a lot of Experience with imagination; Including Legends, Fairy tales, and Believes. However, behind every Story is a truth. In this case the truth Behind the story is that you have to take a Risk, to accomplish a fact that you can pass on as a knowledge.

There are over thousands of plants that can harm or kill you, And now imagine you wouldn't know about that. As an example, How far would your imagination go if you'd see red berries on side bushes not knowing that they are poisoned? That persons mind must of had split decisions, as he trusted his imagination of it to be a tasteful berry and ate it. Most likely it got the person sick and ended up dying, but thats the Risk the person took to acknowledge fellow men that it's is not edible.

Science Labs, Probably the most enjoyable part of HighSchool. The reason why doing Hands-on Activities is so important is because we are actually able to see what we learn. A Human is not capable of knowing the effect of a cause without imagining a solution that is able to turn out as an acknowledging fact.

"Imagination is more important than Knowledge." Scientist Albert Einstein said. My position on this Statement stands on agreeing to what he had once said due to the 3 examples i have listed. Knowledge doesn't come with Birth, it comes with the Risks your willing to take, the experience you make, and the Imagination you have.

official_overall_rubric.5: Native-like facility in the use of language with syntactic variety, Appropriate word choice and phrases; well-controlled text organization; precise use of grammar and conventions; rare language inaccuracies that do not impede communication.
official_overall_rubric.4: Facility in the use of language with syntactic variety and range of words and phrases; controlled organization; accuracy in grammar and conventions; occasional language inaccuracies that rarely impede communication.
official_overall_rubric.3: Facility limited to the use of common structures and generic vocabulary; organization generally controlled although connection sometimes absent or unsuccessful; errors in grammar and syntax and usage. Communication is impeded by language inaccuracies in some cases.
official_overall_rubric.2: Inconsistent facility in sentence formation, word choice, and mechanics; organization partially developed but may be missing or unsuccessful. Communication impeded in many instances by language inaccuracies.
official_overall_rubric.1: A limited range of familiar words or phrases loosely strung together; frequent errors in grammar (including syntax) and usage. Communication impeded in most cases by language inaccuracies.
